section: Important flagship programmes of the Central Government - agriculture, rural, urban, employment, skilling
subsections: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G
Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP
Scheme → nodal ministry and funding pattern

accepted.s: With reference to the employment guarantee framework in rural areas, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: VB-G RAM G — 100 days of work per household per year
MGNREGA — 100 days of unskilled manual work per household per year
VB-G RAM G — 75 days of skilled work per household per year
MGNREGA — 125 days of work per household per year
accepted.x: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days of unskilled manual work per household per year, whereas VB-G RAM G provides a 125-day guarantee.
accepted.tq: Use the comparison table to distinguish the changed numerical guarantee.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding VB-G RAM G:
1. It replaces MGNREGA.
2. It provides a guarantee of 125 days of work per household.
3. It is implemented by Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. VB-G RAM G replaces MGNREGA, raises the guarantee to 125 days and is implemented through Panchayati Raj Institutions.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the status, guarantee and implementing-body rows.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the status of MGNREGA in relation to VB-G RAM G?
o: MGNREGA has been repealed and replaced by VB-G RAM G
MGNREGA was merged with PMEGP
MGNREGA was converted into a Centrally Sponsored Scheme without repeal
MGNREGA continues unchanged alongside VB-G RAM G
accepted.x: MGNREGA is stated to have been repealed and replaced by VB-G RAM G.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between continuation, merger and repeal.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Presidential assent to the VB-G RAM G legislation was given on:
o: 20 December 2025
16 December 2025
1 July 2026
accepted.x: The legislation received Presidential assent on 20 December 2025. It was notified on 11 May 2026 and came into force on 1 July 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the introduction, assent, notification and commencement dates.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events relating to VB-G RAM G in chronological order:
A. The Act came into force
B. The Act was introduced
C. Presidential assent was given
D. The Act was notified
o: B, C, D, A
C, B, D, A
B, D, C, A
D, C, B, A
accepted.x: The sequence is introduction on 16 December 2025, assent on 20 December 2025, notification on 11 May 2026 and commencement on 1 July 2026.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last dates, then arrange the intermediate milestones.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: VB-G RAM G is the abbreviated form of:
o: Viksit Bharat—Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin)
Viksit Bharat—Gram Rozgar and Awas Mission
Viksit Bharat—Gramin Rehabilitation and Manufacturing Mission
Village Bharat—Guarantee for Rural Agriculture and Migration
accepted.x: VB-G RAM G stands for Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin).
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of the scheme acronym.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The tagline of VB-G RAM G is:
o: Kaushal Bhi, Awas Bhi
Shram Bhi, Suraksha Bhi
Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi
Sabka Rozgar, Sabka Vikas
accepted.x: The stated tagline of VB-G RAM G is “Rozgar Bhi, Samman Bhi”.
accepted.tq: Recall the official slogan rather than the scheme objective.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under MGNREGA, unemployment allowance was payable when work was not provided within:
o: 7 days
10 days
15 days
30 days
accepted.x: MGNREGA provided for unemployment allowance if work was not given within 15 days, and the allowance was paid by the States.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise statutory time limit and the responsible level of government.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding MGNREGA is correct?
o: The Gram Sabha conducted the social audit and one-third of workers had to be women.
The Lok Sabha conducted the social audit and half of workers had to be women.
The State Legislature conducted the social audit and one-fourth of workers had to be women.
The Ministry of Finance conducted the social audit and women had no specified share.
accepted.x: Under MGNREGA, the Gram Sabha ran the social audit, and one-third of workers were required to be women.
accepted.tq: Match the function and reservation-like participation requirement with the correct institution.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: MGNREGA is associated with which of the following Sustainable Development Goals?
o: SDG 5 and SDG 16
SDG 2 and SDG 14
SDG 1 and SDG 8
SDG 6 and SDG 13
accepted.x: MGNREGA is linked to SDG 1, No Poverty, and SDG 8, Decent Work.
accepted.tq: Test the scheme-to-SDG relationship directly.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Section 4(5) of VB-G RAM G, who fixes the State-wise normative allocations?
o: The State Election Commission
The Gram Sabha
The Centre
The Finance Commission
accepted.x: Section 4(5) provides that the Centre fixes State-wise normative allocations.
accepted.tq: Use the “who would do this job?” method for allocation powers.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched regarding funding under VB-G RAM G?
o: All Union Territories, including those with legislatures, receive 100 per cent Central funding
The scheme is a Central Sector scheme in every State
States bear the entire wage and material expenditure in all areas
The Centre-State ratio is generally 60:40, with 90:10 for the North-Eastern and Himalayan States
accepted.x: VB-G RAM G follows a 60:40 pattern generally and 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States; Union Territories without legislatures receive 100 per cent Central funding.
accepted.tq: Compare the normal, special-region and Union Territory funding ratios.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under VB-G RAM G, the allowance and delay compensation are borne:
o: Fully by the States
By the Gram Panchayats from own revenues
Equally by the Centre and the States
Entirely by the Centre
accepted.x: The allowance and delay compensation under VB-G RAM G are borne fully by the States.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the funding responsibility for compensation from the general cost-sharing pattern.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the financial figures stated for VB-G RAM G?
o: Total allocation ₹95,692.31 crore; Centre’s share ₹1,51,282 crore
Total allocation ₹1,25,000 crore; Centre’s share ₹75,000 crore
Total allocation ₹1,51,282 crore; Centre’s share ₹95,692.31 crore
Total allocation ₹2,50,000 crore; Centre’s share ₹1,51,282 crore
accepted.x: The total amount stated is ₹1,51,282 crore, of which the Centre’s share is ₹95,692.31 crore.
accepted.tq: Read the total and component figures without reversing their order.
accepted.sec: Employment - MGNREGA features, now VB-G RAM G  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. PM Vishwakarma — Ministry of MSME
2. PM-AJAY — Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
3. PM SVANidhi — Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
4. PMEGP — Khadi and Village Industries Commission as nodal agency
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. PM Vishwakarma is under MSME, PM-AJAY under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, PM SVANidhi under MoHUA, and KVIC is the nodal agency for PMEGP.
accepted.tq: Use institution–scheme matching and eliminate options containing a swapped ministry.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM Vishwakarma is intended primarily for:
o: Artisans in 18 traditional trades
Rural youth seeking placement-linked employment
SC-majority villages with more than 500 residents
Street vendors in statutory towns
accepted.x: PM Vishwakarma covers artisans in 18 traditional trades and provides identity cards, training, toolkits and credit support.
accepted.tq: Match the programme with its target group rather than its support instrument.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a benefit associated with PM Vishwakarma?
o: ₹500 per day training stipend
Collateral-free credit up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent interest
Working-capital loans beginning at ₹10,000 for street vendors
Toolkit support up to ₹15,000
accepted.x: The ₹10,000 working-capital loan is associated with PM SVANidhi. PM Vishwakarma provides the stipend, toolkit support and collateral-free credit mentioned in the other options.
accepted.tq: Find the benefit belonging to the neighbouring scheme rather than the target scheme.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM-AJAY, introduced in 2021–22, is a:
o: Central Sector scheme for apprenticeships
Centrally Sponsored Scheme for heritage cities
Central Sector scheme for urban street vendors
Centrally Sponsored Scheme for development of SC-majority villages
accepted.x: PM-AJAY is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme of 2021–22 aimed at the development of SC-majority villages.
accepted.tq: Separate the scheme’s target group from urban, apprenticeship and heritage programmes.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Adarsh Gram component of PM-AJAY covers villages having:
o: At least 2,000 people and more than 40 per cent minority population
At least 500 people and more than 40 per cent SC population
At least 1,000 people and more than 25 per cent ST population
Less than 500 people and more than 50 per cent women
accepted.x: The Adarsh Gram component covers villages with 500 or more people and more than 40 per cent Scheduled Caste population.
accepted.tq: Check both qualifying thresholds; a changed threshold makes the option incorrect.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the Adarsh Gram component is correct?
o: It was formerly known as HRIDAY and was started in 2015.
It was formerly known as PMEGP and was started in 2008.
It was formerly known as PMAGY and was started in 2009–10.
It was formerly known as DAY-NULM and was started in 2013.
accepted.x: The Adarsh Gram component was formerly PMAGY, which dates to 2009–10.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar scheme acronyms and their years of origin.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PMEGP is best described as a programme providing:
o: Training and certification under the Skill India Mission
Credit-linked subsidy for new micro-enterprises
Tap water to all households in statutory towns
Loans to street vendors for working capital only
accepted.x: PMEGP, launched in 2008, provides credit-linked subsidy for new micro-enterprises, with KVIC as its nodal agency.
accepted.tq: Match the objective with the correct programme and avoid confusing subsidy with loan-only schemes.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s: PM SVANidhi is associated with which of the following?
o: Loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for greenfield enterprises
Loans to street vendors, including a first loan of ₹10,000 and a 7 per cent interest subsidy
Loans to artisans up to ₹3 lakh at 5 per cent interest
Loans exclusively for SC-majority villages
accepted.x: PM SVANidhi supports street vendors through working-capital loans; the first loan is ₹10,000 and the scheme provides a 7 per cent interest subsidy and digital cashback.
accepted.tq: Separate similar credit schemes by beneficiary, initial loan and interest support.
accepted.sec: Central programme objectives → scheme  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. AMRUT 2.0 — Tap water to all households in statutory towns
2. Smart Cities Mission — Technology-led transformation of 100 cities
3. HRIDAY — Heritage development in 12 cities
4. PM e-Bus Sewa — 10,000 e-buses on PPP for city bus services
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. They represent the stated objectives and scale of the respective urban programmes.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive numbers—100 cities, 12 cities and 10,000 buses—to verify the pairs.
accepted.sec: Urban programmes → objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The budget allocation for SBM-Urban 2.0 was stated to have been halved to which amount in 2026–27?
o: ₹1,000 crore
₹2,000 crore
₹2,500 crore
₹5,000 crore
accepted.x: The 2026–27 budget allocation for SBM-Urban 2.0 was stated to have been halved to ₹2,500 crore.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise revised amount rather than the original or a rounded distractor.
accepted.sec: Urban programmes → objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Urban Challenge Fund is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under MoHUA involving:
o: ₹1 lakh crore from FY 2025–26 to 2030–31
accepted.x: The Urban Challenge Fund is a ₹1 lakh crore Centrally Sponsored Scheme under MoHUA for FY 2025–26 to 2030–31.
accepted.tq: Combine the amount, ministry and time period; changing any one creates a false option.
accepted.sec: Urban programmes → objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs was formed in 2017 by merging which two ministries?
o: Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation and Urban Development
Housing and Finance and Urban Development
Rural Development and Urban Development
Social Justice and Housing and Urban Affairs
accepted.x: MoHUA was formed in 2017 by merging the Ministry of Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation with the Ministry of Urban Development.
accepted.tq: Test the exact predecessor ministries rather than a related ministry.
accepted.sec: Urban programmes → objective  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Skill India and PMKVY is correct?
o: PMKVY is the flagship of MoHUA for urban infrastructure.
Skill India Mission was launched in 2008 and PMKVY is a rural housing scheme.
Skill India Mission was launched in 2015 and PMKVY is its flagship for short-term training and certification.
Skill India focuses exclusively on long-term university education.
accepted.x: Skill India Mission was launched in 2015, and PMKVY is its flagship programme for short-term training and certification.
accepted.tq: Match the flagship programme with its mission, year and training purpose.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the versions of PMKVY mentioned in the material?
o: PMKVY 1.0, 2.0 and 5.0 only
accepted.x: PMKVY has operated through versions 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 and 4.0.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete numbered series and reject inserted or omitted versions.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s: The nodal ministry for Skill India Mission and PMKVY is:
o: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Rural Development
accepted.x: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship is the nodal ministry for Skill India Mission and PMKVY.
accepted.tq: Apply the ministry–programme matching method.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Skill India Digital Hub is:
o: A digital payments platform for street vendors launched in 2020
A digital skilling platform of MSDE launched in 2023
A MoRD programme for rural self-employment launched in 2008
A World Bank fund for urban infrastructure launched in 2021
accepted.x: Skill India Digital Hub is MSDE’s digital skilling platform, launched in 2023.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the digital skilling platform from digital-payment and infrastructure programmes.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. NAPS — Stipend support for apprentices
2. Jan Shikshan Sansthan — Training of 36.52 lakh people
3. PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana — ₹2,400 crore paid to 15 lakh first-time employees
Which of the pairs given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. NAPS supported stipends for 54.41 lakh apprentices, Jan Shikshan Sansthan trained 36.52 lakh people, and the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana paid ₹2,400 crore to 15 lakh first-time employees.
accepted.tq: Check the programme, beneficiary and quantitative figure together in each statement.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s: SANKALP is best described as a:
o: MoHUA programme providing e-buses to cities
MoRD programme providing self-employment through rural industrial estates
World Bank-supported MSDE programme strengthening district-level skilling institutions
Central Sector scheme providing toolkit grants to artisans
accepted.x: SANKALP is a World Bank-supported programme of MSDE intended to strengthen district-level skilling institutions.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme through its international support, ministry and institutional objective.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the two skilling programmes of the Ministry of Rural Development?
o: DDU-GKY provides artisan toolkits, while RSETIs provide e-buses.
DDU-GKY is placement-linked for rural youth, while RSETIs focus on self-employment.
DDU-GKY focuses on urban street vendors, while RSETIs provide heritage conservation.
DDU-GKY is a World Bank programme, while RSETIs are run by MoHUA.
accepted.x: DDU-GKY is a placement-linked programme for rural youth, whereas RSETIs are associated with self-employment.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two programmes under the same ministry by their livelihood pathway.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s: APSSDC is setting up how many skill hubs in rural colleges with technology firms?
accepted.x: APSSDC is setting up 50 skill hubs in rural colleges in association with technology firms.
accepted.tq: Test the exact State-level programme figure.
accepted.sec: Skilling - PMKVY, Skill India, SIDH, NAPS, SANKALP  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a Central Sector scheme?
o: PMAY-G
PM-AJAY
DAY-NRLM
PM Vishwakarma
accepted.x: PM Vishwakarma is listed as a Central Sector scheme funded and run centrally. DAY-NRLM, PMAY-G and PM-AJAY are Centrally Sponsored examples.
accepted.tq: Separate Central Sector schemes from Centrally Sponsored schemes using the funding pattern.
accepted.sec: Scheme → nodal ministry and funding pattern

accepted.s: Which of the following groups consists entirely of Centrally Sponsored Schemes?
o: PM-KISAN, PM Vishwakarma and SEED
DAY-NRLM, VB-G RAM G, PMAY-G and PM-AJAY
PM-KISAN, DILRMP and PM-AJAY only
SEED, PM Vishwakarma and Urban Challenge Fund only
accepted.x: DAY-NRLM, VB-G RAM G, PMAY-G and PM-AJAY are listed as Centrally Sponsored Schemes. PM-KISAN, PM Vishwakarma, DILRMP and SEED are Central Sector examples, while the Urban Challenge Fund is also Centrally Sponsored.
accepted.tq: Classify the entire group rather than relying on one familiar scheme.
accepted.sec: Scheme → nodal ministry and funding pattern

accepted.s: The general funding pattern for Centrally Sponsored Schemes, as stated, is:
o: 40:60, with the Centre bearing the smaller share in special States
60:40, 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States, and 100 per cent for Union Territories without legislatures
100 per cent Centre for all schemes
50:50 for all States and 75:25 for Union Territories
accepted.x: The general pattern is 60:40, changing to 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan States and 100 per cent Central funding for Union Territories without legislatures.
accepted.tq: Remember the normal ratio and its two specified exceptions.
accepted.sec: Scheme → nodal ministry and funding pattern

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Urban Challenge Fund — Central Sector scheme with 100 per cent Central funding
SEED — Central Sector scheme
DILRMP — Central Sector scheme since 2016
PM-KISAN — Central Sector scheme
accepted.x: The Urban Challenge Fund is listed as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, not a Central Sector scheme with universal 100 per cent Central funding. PM-KISAN, DILRMP since 2016 and SEED are Central Sector examples.
accepted.tq: Find the scheme whose funding classification has been swapped.
accepted.sec: Scheme → nodal ministry and funding pattern
